hesitations.reason: The High or Medium tie-break applies only when no official text settles a contradicted point. On the bayonet, the official manual (and CNCNZ, which repeats it) says one thing, while the wiki and the 1.04 data say the opposite. I read the outdated manual as not settling it, because the game data contradict it. The point decides whether the unit has a second weapon entry, so I dropped to medium. If the manual counts as settling the point, the level would be high, but the entry would then need a bayonet weapon.

hesitations.reason: The rule is clear but the sources are not: official text (manual p34) against the wiki's trivia and the 1.04 weapon set, command set and Weapon.ini. Recorded in uncertain with sources_disagree.
The engineer tie-break asks for enemy buildings taken over and kept. Capture Building does that, but only after an upgrade, so engineer ranks at step 5 rather than step 2.

Active or Channel tie-break: the capture runs a long time and the Capture building page says moving or dying ends it, which is channel's 'stops if you move or are interrupted'. Read as a timed action that runs to its end, it would be active.
The rule was clear: SpecialPower.ini and CNCNZ both give 15 s, exactly on the short/medium edge, and an edge value takes the higher band.

The registry's Generals notes and the task say no pattern. research/registry-notes/patterns.md folds the horde bonus into rally-allies, but the pattern-links convention says the pattern's summary wins over that note, and rally-allies needs one unit that raises the others.

Matchups rule 7 says about two to five as a guide, not a cap. Rule 3 allows a unit: link for a same-game rival the source names (the wiki singles out the Ranger's flash-bangs) beside the word-list link.

The rule was clear: the small arms or machine gun tie-break says rifles are always small arms, and the manual and wiki call it a bolt-action rifle. Only the internal 1.04 weapon name says machine gun, and names do not decide families.

Infiltrator's description names shutting down buildings, but the engineer/infiltrator/logistics tie-break says sabotage 'from inside'. The Hacker hacks from a short distance with a virus. I read the virus as sabotage from inside the building's systems. Disabler fails its requires (no control pattern, no stun or silence trait) and its tie-break is about units, so I added no fit_note for it.

The building stays down only while he keeps hacking, and a new order or his death ends it, which fits the Active or Channel tie-break. He also stands still with his laptop unpacked, but the Toggle or Deploy tie-break is about two-state modes, not a targeted hack.

The task asks for the 'sabotage variant', but capture-structure has no variant with that id. The nearest are switch-off (stops a function for a time) and hack-from-range (works from a short distance). Source units record pattern ids only, so no variant is stored. disable-machine is for vehicles and drones, not buildings.

unclear_rules.topic: Confidence tie-break with outdated official text
unclear_rules.note: The High or Medium tie-break applies when 'no official text settles' a contradiction. On the Red Guard's bayonet, official text (the 2003 manual) contradicts the wiki and the 1.04 game data. The rule does not say whether official text the game data disprove still 'settles' the point. If it does, the entry should keep a bayonet weapon at high confidence. I coded medium with no bayonet.

unclear_rules.topic: Pattern variants named in a task
unclear_rules.note: The task asked for capture-structure's 'sabotage variant', but the pattern has no variant with that id (the nearest are switch-off and hack-from-range), and the source-unit schema has no field to record a variant. Only the pattern id is stored.

The engineer/infiltrator/logistics tie-break gives infiltrator for sabotage 'from inside'. A hacker who shuts a building down with a virus from a short distance is not covered either way. The role's own description ('shuts down buildings') fits, so I read the virus as from inside.

unclear_rules.note: The trait says 'a stronger stationary mode', while the deploy-siege-mode summary also covers 'a field or building that works only while it stays put'. It is unclear whether an income-only set-up (the Hacker's laptop) takes the trait. I followed the pattern and the Slave Miner precedent.

unclear_rules.note: The Hacker's building hack re-arms in half a second (CNCNZ: four seconds) but keeps running while he stays at it. The cooldown rule does not say whether a near-instant re-arm on a channel counts as 'no wait' (leave it out) or as spam.

unclear_rules.topic: new_mechanics when a pattern covers only part of an ability
unclear_rules.note: The report schema describes new mechanics as abilities left with an empty patterns list. Hack Internet links deploy-siege-mode for the planting, but its core mechanic (income in place) has no pattern, so I listed it in new_mechanics anyway.

unclear_rules.topic: Horde bonus wording in the registry
unclear_rules.note: The Generals game-wide note says the bonus comes with 'at least four other allied soldiers of any kind'. EA's HordeUpdate.cpp counts only allied units that carry a horde module of their own and match its infantry kind, and the wiki's Horde Bonus page agrees. The Red Guard entry follows the code and records the difference in uncertain.

The registry asks that ranking by hacking be stated in the ability summary. It does not say whether an innate ability whose output rises with rank should also link earn-veterancy; Paired entries ties that link only to weapons that come with a rank. I did not link it.

new_mechanics.summary: Each member of certain unit types fires faster while enough other members stand close by, and none of them grants the bonus to the rest, so the strength comes from staying in a crowd. Counterplay: splash and area weapons such as flash-bang grenades punish the clump, and picking off members or splitting the group breaks the count.

The unit sets up anywhere, with no resource field, haul or drop-off, and sends its team a steady trickle of money for as long as it stays put; it earns more per payment as the work ranks it up. Counterplay: find and kill the stationary, defenceless earner or catch it while it packs up, because there is no route or bank to raid, only the unit itself.

source_problems:
Contradictions between sources, all recorded in uncertain with sources_disagree where they apply:
(1) Red Guard bayonet: the base-game manual (p34) and CNCNZ give him a bayonet for close fighting. The wiki's trivia says it was cut, and the 1.04 files have no bayonet in his weapon set or command set. This drops the Red Guard to medium.
(2) Hacker income rate: the wiki says payments come faster at each rank, up to one a second at Heroic, and CNCNZ gives the base income per second. The 1.04 Object file and EA's HackInternetAIUpdate.cpp keep one fixed interval (two seconds, shorter only inside a building) and raise only the amount per payment, 5/6/8/10.
(3) Hacker building-hack cooldown: SpecialPower.ini gives 0.5 s and CNCNZ gives 4 s. Both band as spam.
(4) Horde bonus: the registry's game-wide note says 'four other allied soldiers of any kind'. HordeUpdate.cpp and the wiki's Horde Bonus page count only Mini-Gunners, Tank Hunters and Red Guards. The Red Guard wiki's strategy text also has Red Guards keeping Battlemasters horded, which the code and the Horde Bonus page contradict.
